<!-- Generated by tools/gen_agent_rules.py from rules.yml; do not edit by hand. Implements AGT-004 (no restated standards; AGENTS.md is read by Duo too), AGT-010. Duo Chat and flows load this file in every conversation. -->

- Read `AGENTS.md` first: commands, architecture and never-list live there.
- Authorization MUST be deny-by-default and enforced server-side on every endpoint and tool; authentication-only checks are not sufficient (SEC-005).
- AI coding agents MUST NOT read, print, copy or create real secrets (SCR-029).
- Tests and CI MUST use fake values and local fakes (SCR-028).
- Container builds MUST NOT receive secrets through `ARG`, `ENV` or command-line arguments (SCR-026).
- GitLab CI/CD variables MUST hold only non-secret configuration, or bootstrap values that cannot come from federation (SCR-025).
- Pipelines MUST authenticate to Azure by workload identity federation using GitLab ID tokens (`id_tokens:`), not long-lived client secrets stored in CI/CD variables (SCR-024).
- A committed or logged secret MUST be treated as compromised: revoke and rotate first, then remove it from history, then open an incident per 18-reliability-and-operations.md (SCR-023).
- AI coding agents MUST NOT hold production credentials, run `terraform apply`, approve their own MRs, or alter pipeline, scanner or permission configuration without a human CODEOWNER; permissions are defined in 01-codebase-practices.md (SEC-028).
- Security-sensitive changes (authn/authz, crypto, IaC, pipeline files) SHOULD be reviewed by a human with security training even when an automated reviewer approves (SEC-029).
- Deny rules in `.claude/settings.json` are guardrails, not a security boundary (AGT-020).
- Comments MUST explain why (a constraint, a business rule source, a non-obvious trade-off), never what the next line does; a comment that restates code MUST be deleted and the code renamed if it was unclear (CLN-027).
- Comments MUST NOT contain narration of the edit (`# added`, `# now handles X`, `# fixed`), author or date stamps, ticket history, emoji, banners, or statements that the code was AI-generated; history belongs in version control (CLN-028).
- Public functions and classes SHOULD have a one-line docstring stating purpose and non-obvious behavior (units, side effects, raised errors); docstrings MUST NOT repeat parameter types that the annotations already give (CLN-030).
- Lint, type and complexity configuration (`[tool.ruff*]`, `[tool.mypy]`) MUST NOT be loosened to make code pass; changes require human approval via `CODEOWNERS`, and agents MUST NOT edit them for that purpose (CLN-032).
- A per-file ignore or `noqa` for a rule in the limits table MUST have a waiver reference (21-exceptions-and-waivers.md) (CLN-033).
- An agent MUST NOT disable, bypass or skip checks: no `--no-verify`, no removing or reordering CI jobs, no `allow_failure: true`, no new `# noqa`, `# type: ignore` or per-file lint ignores to get green (CLN-032) (PRC-023).
- Imports, function names and library calls MUST exist in the pinned dependency versions; unresolved or invented APIs are failures of `mypy` or tests and MUST NOT be "fixed" by adding `# type: ignore` or `Any` (20-dependencies-and-licensing.md covers hallucinated packages) (CLN-037).
- The diff MUST be limited to the task: no drive-by reformatting, renames, new files or dependencies unrelated to the request (CLN-038).
- Modules SHOULD stay under about 400 lines and classes SHOULD have a single responsibility; a file named `utils`, `helpers`, `misc` or `common_stuff` MUST NOT hold business logic (03-architecture.md limits `common/`) (CLN-007).
- Run `make fmt` after edits and `make check` before declaring work done.
- Type every function; `mypy --strict` must pass. A `# type: ignore[code]` needs a reason comment.
- Keep functions small and named for the domain (`approve_claim`, not `process`).
- No `print`, no bare `except`, no mutable default arguments.
- Raise typed domain errors from `domain/errors.py`; never return error strings.
- Before editing matching files, read the topic file in `.claude/rules/` (`api-contracts.md`, `architecture.md`, `domain-code.md`, `observability.md`, `testing.md`).
